Uncaptured: Odyssey of a whistleblower, Mosilo Mothepo

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Mosilo Mothepo is one of the most important state capture whistleblowers - her odyssey is one of triumph over adversity. She has been through hell but her faith and her family saw her through it

Unique Selling Point:
A one on one interview with Mosilo Mothepo who has stayed mostly out of the public eye
Never before facts revealed about Nene Gate and the main actors like Eric Wood
Two strong black female narratives that intertwined and held up a beacon of light when dark and powerful forces arrayed against them
footage of the events spoken about
Timeous because Mosilo's story was one of those instrumental in Thuli Madonsela recommending the state capture commission which now comes to an end

Summary:
Uncaptured – Mosilo Mothepo’ story

For more than three years I have tried periodically to get Mosilo Mothepu to speak to Carte Blanche. She is the Nenegate / Trillian whistleblower and one of the most important voices in the state capture saga. First she was terrified and refused to show her face – then she had a nervous breakdown. Unable to find a job her life was in a downward spiral – and after several attempts – I gave up. Now she has written her story and is prepared finally to give Carte Blanche that interview. The forward is written by Thuli Madonsela who plays an integral part in Mosilo’s story as it was Madonsela that took the call from Mosilo when she first made the decision to spill the beans on holiday in Egypt.

Further information:
Here is an extract from Thuli Madonsela
“Whistle-blowers are brave people who risk everything to bring what happened in the dark into the light. Mosilo went beyond the call of duty when she contacted me from Egypt, where she was holidaying, and offered to tell me what had happened between Eskom and Trillian, a company of which she was a CEO at the time. Her information pertained to the firing of Nhlanhla Nene as minister of finance and his subsequent replacement with Des van Rooyen.
I could not believe it, till Mosilo met with me and my team at our regular spot where we congregated for such encounters. Her cell-phone text messages and emails proved that Trillian knew Nene was on his way out, and that a person who was going to open opportunities for the company was on his way in.
Mosilo gave us a folder that mapped out a broader state-capture spider web and provided leads for our investigation. Time limits constrained the investigation team’s ability to authenticate those emails as per the Standard Operating Protocol (SOP) I had designed for valid Public Protector investigations.
Nevertheless, the value of Mosilo’s evidence was not lost. It became one of the pieces of the puzzle that buttressed my belief that we needed a commission of inquiry to conclude the investigation.



Mosilo Mothepo was outed to a newspapers prematurely, she has been harassed and prosecuted by the Hawks and her patriotism was met with betrayal which caused her immeasurable pain. As a result of her story Madonsela herself is recommending protection of whistleblowers to ensure no-one goes through what she has been through. But through her ordeal the one thing that Mosilo managed to hold onto was her faith, and it is that that enabled her to come through eventually – as Madonsela says:
“I have yet to meet another person with faith like Mosilo’s. Her story proves that if you resolutely stand for the truth, you may face painful and immeasurable pushback, but you will prevail in the end. It also proves that you cannot live a life that is incongruent with your soul truth. As Martin Luther King Jr once said, ‘The moral arch of the universe may be long, but it always bends towards justice.’
What makes this story a Carte Blanche winner is that we covered the Nenegate story at the time and we still have all the footage and interviews – including the interview with Pravin Gordhan, the newspapers that morning on the pavement in Pretoria announcing his axing etc etc. Also can be done relatively quickly and is a perfect story as the commission ploughs through Eskom evidence

FINAL SCRIPT UNCAPTURED FOR TX 11 APRIL 2021

Masilo up sound over typing
I wrote this book to tell my story, to reveal the effects of state capture on ordinary people, to draw attention to the role of the whistleblower, and the danger and devastation we face...

Fade to black

Commentary One
South Africa 2015. In high places there were many dark secrets. State owned enterprises were the target of State capture networks, but the true picture was still hidden.

Mosilo Mothepu had just joined Regiments, a financial advisory firm, enticed by director Eric Wood who asked her to lead a big Eskom project

Mosilo
And they wanted me to head up that team, so for me it was very exciting- I mean he gave me a blank cheque, can we afford you, sign on bonus and I happily went.

LINK
These were once the offices of Regiments. They were rich and riding the wave, shaking down the SOE’s writes Mothepu, as they extracted massive fees from the SOE’S

Mosilo
They were making a lot of money, plus Eric liked fast cars ..Aston Martin ...he had a helicopter, he had a farm.

Commentary two
As a financial advisory, Regiments would structure loans- if for example Eskom needed billions to complete Kusile and Medupi, or when Transnet wanted to buy new locomotives, or SA express needed finance. They also said they could help the State owned companies cut costs

Masa
If you had to off the top of your head quantify exactly how much was given to Regiments and later Trillian for consulting what do you think it would be?
Mosilo
So I would probably say two to three billion
Masa:
of South African taxpayers money?
Mosilo
Yes, with nothing to show. It's just advice.




Commentary three
Mothepu has finance degrees, and her career was her life. She bought her own Sandton home, she worked long hours and often shared an early morning coffee with her boss Eric Wood.

Mosilo
One Monday morning, the 26th of October and he looks like the cat that has all the cream, he is in his three piece suit, and then he says the president is going to fire Nhlanhla Nene, and in my mind I don’t understand the significance of this. Why are you telling me about a reshuffle?

Commentary four
Six weeks later, former President Zuma did fire Nene. In came the unknown Des Van Rooyen. Markets tumbled

Mosilo
I think we lost R500 billion in your equity your pensions your bonds, it was devastating the currency was gone, the bond markets
Masa
The original plan was to have Des Van Rooyen
Mosilo
Yes pliable that is what Eric said. The reason why Nene had to go, was that he was not approving the nuclear deal, and there were certain transactions that the minister would be more pliable to these transactions

Commentary Five
But around the same time, boardroom battles at Regiments led to a split. Eric Wood left to start Trillian, with the man known as the fourth Gupta brother- Salim Essa

AmaBhungane’ Susan Comrie investigated both companies

Susan how significant a role did Regiments and Trillian play in State Capture
Susan
They were absolutely crucial, we had described Regiments as the trojan horse which had allowed the Guptas to come into various state owned entities. Very often the companies that the Gupta’s were using to extract tens of millions, hundreds of millions from SOE’s, they were just letterboxes, so they really needed some kind of a credible front, and that credible front became Regiments and then later Trillian

Commentary Six
Mothepu went with Eric Wood as the new CEO of Trillian. Eskom’s top bosses were now her clients.
Masa
Eric Wood was taking you everywhere what was that like ?
Mosilo
It was intoxicating it was like having a seat at the table, and not even lean in you were saying this is my new CEO, and they were saying you take transformation seriously , and to be in the forefront of these industry leaders that I thought at the time were taking SA’s economy forward

Commentary Seven
Within months though, Mothepu began to realize she was being played
Mosilo
It was grooming and fronting.
Masa
So in theory you were the CEO but there were these three white guys and Salim Essa running the show?
Mosilo
Exactly! And to make it worse I was a director, so I had to comply with the companies act,
so I felt I was just there to look black and female and to be paraded around and that was very, very disempowering

Commentary eight
And her big bonuses began to make sense

Mosilo
In my book there is a specific chill that goes down my spine when I remember this conversation, and Eric said to me, be loyal to me, and I will reward you. So he had outpriced me out of the market, and my bonuses were the types that used to pay off mortgages

Commentary nine
And buy designer handbags.

Masa
So this is the Eric Wood bag?
Mosilo
This is grooming bag. So I think it signifies that stage in my life where I was his blue eyed wonder, and I was going to Paris on a conference and he gave me such a wonderful huge stipend, so I think this bag is the beginning of the many other stories of bags you will see in my book – every single one of them has a meaning.

Masa
In the book, you also describe Eric as the mastermind, architect and enabler of the grandest looting and state capture imaginable?
Mosilo
That's one hundred percent.

Commentary ten
She wanted us to meet at her home to show Carte Blanche that whistle-blowers are just ordinary people
Mosilo
And I just wanted to show SA that we are not extraordinary, we are vain we have guilty pleasures we are not vegetarian vegans hugging trees. You just have to have the courage and courage comes from all areas of life

Commentary eleven
Eric Wood declined to comment on any of these allegations.

As 2016 unfolded, the Gupta’s seemed unstoppable and AmaBhungane connected the dots in a Mail and Guardian expose

Mosilo
Wow, that was the day I realized that I was part of something very evil, and it had various players within the State owned companies, but I realised I can actually fill in the blanks

Commentary twelve
Also trying to fill in the blanks was former public protector Thuli Madonsela, who was in a race against time to complete her state of Capture Report, before her term ended

LINK
Mothepu knew she could fill in the gaps and really help Thuli Madonsela with her state of capture report, and she had a trail of hard evidence

Mosilo
And I finally saw her terms of reference and I saw I could help her on 80% of these things.
I had a moment of introspection, who are you and I said no I am not a minister. Somebody else will tell her, not me- I don’t have protection. And then I remembered a verse, the only thing necessary for evil to triumph is for good women or men to do nothing and I said God give me the strength I have to be a good woman.

Commentary 13
On holiday in Egypt, at a monastery in the desert, she made the decision to tell Thuli Madonsela what she knew

Mosilo
I felt very spiritual, because I felt so broken and lost and so for me it was like reconnecting with god

Susan
The point at which she came to the public protector, it was so crucial, her timing was so, so important. There was a lot of fear and suspicion that state capture was happening but very people had been able to put the proof out there. and Mosilo comes along and she was the person in the room, and not just for Nenegate, she was in the room, had seen what was happening at Regiments and then at Trillian

Commentary Fourteen
Mothepo wanted to remain anonymous but when her CCMA statement was leaked, Eric Wood charged her criminally

Masa
You say Eric wood went into a Stalingrad approach what did he do?
Mosilo
According to the Trillian leaks he spent R18 million on me, fighting Stalingrad, every house, every street every room. It was the 9 criminal charges-cybercrime that was my favourite- laugh -cybercrime because I forwarded some of the emails to my GMAIL account
Masa
Which would later become crucial evidence?
Mosilo
Yes that even the PP and Zondo commission is relying on

Commentary 15
She tried to get a job but corporate South Africa turned their back on her

Mosilo
People were doubting my integrity, jokes like we need three references just don’t ask the Gupta brothers

Commentary 16
With no job and a legal bill north of a million rand, she was about to lose everything she had worked for
Mosilo
I felt like I was fighting alone
Masa
And this home that we sit in now became your wilderness and you isolated here
Mosilo
Absolutely! I lived in my bedroom for two years

Commentary 17
But then the first of her angels she says, showed up. It was French human rights advocate William Bourdon who founded the Platform to Protect whistleblowers in Africa. They settled her legal bill

Mosilo
And you have this organization who support Edward Snowden and Julian Assange and they fly in and come and say we have just opened an office and you are the first African whistleblower and I said to God now I have Euro’s ...David and Goliath lets go

FBI LINK
Many times she felt she was living someone else’s life – like the day she visited the American embassy, not to get a visa but to meet with the FBI

Mosilo
In my journey there is a lot of pinching and I am asking - and I will say this in Sotho:
“Sotho girl what have you done that the FBI wants to see” you but I am happy that my testimony gave way for a sanction list – so Gupta banned with doing business with American corporates and banks


Commentary 18
It was only after the leadership changed at the Hawks and the NPA , that finally all charges against her were dropped, but Mothepu was still without an income

Mosilo
By that time I was angry with God
Masa
You say you had exited the God WhatsApp group as you put it in your book
Mosilo
Yes, I said you have forsaken me, I have stopped applying for jobs I was completely hopeless and out of the blue angels start coming

Commentary 19
He was an angel South Africans knew well, then Deputy Editor of the Financial Mail Sikonathi Mantshantsha who had exposed Eskom corruption. He didn’t know her, but he gave her a call any way

Sikonathi
And she was about to become homeless and no-one was doing a thing about it

Commentary 20
So he wrote an opinion piece – The cost of being principled. Soon afterwards, former MTN CEO Rob Shuter offered her a job.

Masa
One of your angels Sikonathi, had it not been for that piece he wrote things wouldn’t have gone the way they did
Mosilo
Absolutely. That is when I had to with my tail between my legs, applied to rejoin the God WhatsApp group

Commentary 21
But she still had a long way to go. After a nervous breakdown it was her faith, her mom and intense counselling that eventually led to her recovery.

Mosilo
When I look back now I see Trillian, their strategy was to burn me with defamation, assassination of character with bankrupting me and indeed the flames came, but what they forgot is that fire has two properties- fire is painful because it removes the chaff, the impurities your pride. I am not a CEO anymore who am I? and then what they didn’t bargain for is that I came out stronger ready to take on the world

Commentary 22
Finally, almost five years after leaving Trillian, she gave her testimony to the Zondo commission and appealed to it to relook at our treatment of whistleblowers

Mosilo reading
There were times I prayed for death, for peace, times I could have cracked and when I thought I would, but I didn’t. I kept my faith and I made it through, I fought hard and refused to let them take my mental and physical health from me. If you have faith and you stay your course you will triumph.

THE END 14 23

PROMO ONE
For years Mosilo Mothepu tried to stay out of the headlines. Now she has written her story as one of South Africa’s most crucial whistleblowers on the state capture networks

PROMO TWO
The cost of blowing the whistle in South Africa is high. Mosilo Mothepu the Nenegate whistleblower was criminally charged, faced bankruptcy and a breakdown before she triumphed

PROMO THREE
Thuli Madonsela calls her courageous, The platform to protect whistleblowers in Africa calls her the Edward Snowden of South Africa. Mosilo Mothepu blew the whistle on state capture

Masa In the book, you also describe Eric as the mastermind, architect and enabler of the grandest looting and state capture imaginable? Mosilo That's one hundred percent. Commentary ten She wanted us to meet at her home to show Carte Blanche that whistle-blowers are just ordinary people Mosilo And I just wanted to show SA that we are not extraordinary, we are vain we have guilty pleasures we are not vegetarian vegans hugging trees. You just have to have the courage and courage comes from all areas of life Commentary eleven Eric Wood declined to comment on any of these allegations. As 2016 unfolded, the Gupta’s seemed unstoppable and AmaBhungane connected the dots in a Mail and Guardian expose Mosilo Wow, that was the day I realized that I was part of something very evil, and it had various players within the State owned companies, but I realised I can actually fill in the blanks Commentary twelve Also trying to fill in the blanks was former public protector Thuli Madonsela, who was in a race against time to complete her state of Capture Report, before her term ended LINK Mothepu knew she could fill in the gaps and really help Thuli Madonsela with her state of capture report, and she had a trail of hard evidence Mosilo And I finally saw her terms of reference and I saw I could help her on 80% of these things. I had a moment of introspection, who are you and I said no I am not a minister. Somebody else will tell her, not me- I don’t have protection. And then I remembered a verse, the only thing necessary for evil to triumph is for good women or men to do nothing and I said God give me the strength I have to be a good woman. Commentary 13 On holiday in Egypt, at a monastery in the desert, she made the decision to tell Thuli Madonsela what she knew Mosilo I felt very spiritual, because I felt so broken and lost and so for me it was like reconnecting with god Susan The point at which she came to the public protector, it was so crucial, her timing was so, so important. There was a lot of fear and suspicion that state capture was happening but very people had been able to put the proof out there. and Mosilo comes along and she was the person in the room, and not just for Nenegate, she was in the room, had seen what was happening at Regiments and then at Trillian Commentary Fourteen Mothepo wanted to remain anonymous but when her CCMA statement was leaked, Eric Wood charged her criminally Masa You say Eric wood went into a Stalingrad approach what did he do? Mosilo According to the Trillian leaks he spent R18 million on me, fighting Stalingrad, every house, every street every room. It was the 9 criminal charges-cybercrime that was my favourite- laugh -cybercrime because I forwarded some of the emails to my GMAIL account Masa Which would later become crucial evidence? Mosilo Yes that even the PP and Zondo commission is relying on Commentary 15 She tried to get a job but corporate South Africa turned their back on her Mosilo People were doubting my integrity, jokes like we need three references just don’t ask the Gupta brothers Commentary 16 With no job and a legal bill north of a million rand, she was about to lose everything she had worked for Mosilo I felt like I was fighting alone Masa And this home that we sit in now became your wilderness and you isolated here Mosilo Absolutely! I lived in my bedroom for two years Commentary 17 But then the first of her angels she says, showed up. It was French human rights advocate William Bourdon who founded the Platform to Protect whistleblowers in Africa. They settled her legal bill Mosilo And you have this organization who support Edward Snowden and Julian Assange and they fly in and come and say we have just opened an office and you are the first African whistleblower and I said to God now I have Euro’s ...David and Goliath lets go FBI LINK Many times she felt she was living someone else’s life – like the day she visited the American embassy, not to get a visa but to meet with the FBI Mosilo In my journey there is a lot of pinching and I am asking - and I will say this in Sotho: “Sotho girl what have you done that the FBI wants to see” you but I am happy that my testimony gave way for a sanction list – so Gupta banned with doing business with American corporates and banks Commentary 18 It was only after the leadership changed at the Hawks and the NPA , that finally all charges against her were dropped, but Mothepu was still without an income Mosilo By that time I was angry with God Masa You say you had exited the God WhatsApp group as you put it in your book Mosilo Yes, I said you have forsaken me, I have stopped applying for jobs I was completely hopeless and out of the blue angels start coming Commentary 19 He was an angel South Africans knew well, then Deputy Editor of the Financial Mail Sikonathi Mantshantsha who had exposed Eskom corruption. He didn’t know her, but he gave her a call any way Sikonathi And she was about to become homeless and no-one was doing a thing about it Commentary 20 So he wrote an opinion piece – The cost of being principled. Soon afterwards, former MTN CEO Rob Shuter offered her a job. Masa One of your angels Sikonathi, had it not been for that piece he wrote things wouldn’t have gone the way they did Mosilo Absolutely. That is when I had to with my tail between my legs, applied to rejoin the God WhatsApp group Commentary 21 But she still had a long way to go. After a nervous breakdown it was her faith, her mom and intense counselling that eventually led to her recovery. Mosilo When I look back now I see Trillian, their strategy was to burn me with defamation, assassination of character with bankrupting me and indeed the flames came, but what they forgot is that fire has two properties- fire is painful because it removes the chaff, the impurities your pride. I am not a CEO anymore who am I? and then what they didn’t bargain for is that I came out stronger ready to take on the world Commentary 22 Finally, almost five years after leaving Trillian, she gave her testimony to the Zondo commission and appealed to it to relook at our treatment of whistleblowers Mosilo reading There were times I prayed for death, for peace, times I could have cracked and when I thought I would, but I didn’t. I kept my faith and I made it through, I fought hard and refused to let them take my mental and physical health from me. If you have faith and you stay your course you will triumph. THE END 14 23 PROMO ONE For years Mosilo Mothepu tried to stay out of the headlines. Now she has written her story as one of South Africa’s most crucial whistleblowers on the state capture networks PROMO TWO The cost of blowing the whistle in South Africa is high. Mosilo Mothepu the Nenegate whistleblower was criminally charged, faced bankruptcy and a breakdown before she triumphed PROMO THREE Thuli Madonsela calls her courageous, The platform to protect whistleblowers in Africa calls her the Edward Snowden of South Africa. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Mosilo Mothepo is one of the most important state capture whistleblowers - her odyssey is one of triumph over adversity. She has been through hell but her faith and her family saw her through it
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A one on one interview with Mosilo Mothepo who has stayed mostly out of the public eye Never before facts revealed about Nene Gate and the main actors like Eric Wood Two strong black female narratives that intertwined and held up a beacon of light when dark and powerful forces arrayed against them footage of the events spoken about Timeous because Mosilo's story was one of those instrumental in Thuli Madonsela recommending the state capture commission which now comes to an end
metadata.Summary: Uncaptured – Mosilo Mothepo’ story For more than three years I have tried periodically to get Mosilo Mothepu to speak to Carte Blanche. She is the Nenegate / Trillian whistleblower and one of the most important voices in the state capture saga. First she was terrified and refused to show her face – then she had a nervous breakdown. Unable to find a job her life was in a downward spiral – and after several attempts – I gave up. Now she has written her story and is prepared finally to give Carte Blanche that interview. The forward is written by Thuli Madonsela who plays an integral part in Mosilo’s story as it was Madonsela that took the call from Mosilo when she first made the decision to spill the beans on holiday in Egypt.
metadata.Further information: Here is an extract from Thuli Madonsela “Whistle-blowers are brave people who risk everything to bring what happened in the dark into the light. Mosilo went beyond the call of duty when she contacted me from Egypt, where she was holidaying, and offered to tell me what had happened between Eskom and Trillian, a company of which she was a CEO at the time. Her information pertained to the firing of Nhlanhla Nene as minister of finance and his subsequent replacement with Des van Rooyen. I could not believe it, till Mosilo met with me and my team at our regular spot where we congregated for such encounters. Her cell-phone text messages and emails proved that Trillian knew Nene was on his way out, and that a person who was going to open opportunities for the company was on his way in. Mosilo gave us a folder that mapped out a broader state-capture spider web and provided leads for our investigation. Time limits constrained the investigation team’s ability to authenticate those emails as per the Standard Operating Protocol (SOP) I had designed for valid Public Protector investigations. Nevertheless, the value of Mosilo’s evidence was not lost. It became one of the pieces of the puzzle that buttressed my belief that we needed a commission of inquiry to conclude the investigation. Mosilo Mothepo was outed to a newspapers prematurely, she has been harassed and prosecuted by the Hawks and her patriotism was met with betrayal which caused her immeasurable pain. As a result of her story Madonsela herself is recommending protection of whistleblowers to ensure no-one goes through what she has been through. But through her ordeal the one thing that Mosilo managed to hold onto was her faith, and it is that that enabled her to come through eventually – as Madonsela says: “I have yet to meet another person with faith like Mosilo’s. Her story proves that if you resolutely stand for the truth, you may face painful and immeasurable pushback, but you will prevail in the end. It also proves that you cannot live a life that is incongruent with your soul truth. As Martin Luther King Jr once said, ‘The moral arch of the universe may be long, but it always bends towards justice.’ What makes this story a Carte Blanche winner is that we covered the Nenegate story at the time and we still have all the footage and interviews – including the interview with Pravin Gordhan, the newspapers that morning on the pavement in Pretoria announcing his axing etc etc. Also can be done relatively quickly and is a perfect story as the commission ploughs through Eskom evidence
